sketches.title: Ward Round
sketches.premise: You and your opponent are rival doctors on a hospital ward. Each turn, name one standing thing in the ward that treats, blocks, or fixes what your opponent just put before you; the judge decides whether your treatment really works.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes the standing thing by directly treating, disabling, containing, or repairing it, while merely avoiding it, surviving it, or making a larger version of its own kind fails.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and your clinical action: "I am a plaster cast, locking the broken bone still." A cast beats a broken bone.
sketches.first_card: I am a fever, burning through the ward.

sketches.title: Bedside Chain
sketches.premise: The ward has one dangerous problem at a time, and you must hand the next clinician a tool or treatment that solves it. On every turn, your new standing item must act on the previous one, so a tidy chain can become a very untidy emergency.
sketches.criterion: The new item beats the old one by a plain hospital action such as cleaning, cutting, sealing, numbing, feeding, or removing it; hiding, enduring, or offering a stronger duplicate does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name one hospital thing and its action: "I am soap, washing the blood away." Soap beats blood.
sketches.first_card: I am a wound, open and leaking.

sketches.title: Triage Takedown
sketches.premise: You are sorting rival emergencies at the nurses' station. Each turn, name a hospital object, symptom, or treatment that makes the previous thing harmless, and give one short reason before the judge calls the case.
sketches.criterion: A move wins only if it changes, stops, or safely contains the thing in front of it; merely being tougher, farther away, or from the same problem family is a failed discharge.
sketches.move_shape: Give a label and a verdict: "I am an oxygen mask, forcing air into the blocked lungs." The mask beats blocked lungs.
sketches.first_card: I am a blocked airway, stealing every breath.

sketches.title: Scrub Room
sketches.premise: Two teams race through a hospital's scrub room, building a chain of practical fixes. Your turn must be a standing hospital thing that acts on the last thing named, from a mop meeting a spill to a bandage meeting a cut.
sketches.criterion: The judge accepts a direct cleanup, repair, restraint, or removal, but rejects dodging, simply lasting longer, and a bigger or flashier member of the same family as the standing thing.
sketches.move_shape: Use one sentence: "I am a mop, soaking up the spilled medicine." A mop beats spilled medicine.
sketches.first_card: I am spilled medicine, spreading under the beds.

sketches.title: Night Shift
sketches.premise: At midnight, the ward's problems wake up and challenge the night nurse. Each turn, become one clear hospital thing that handles the previous danger by a named action; the lights stay on until a move cannot do its job.
sketches.criterion: The new thing must directly stop, soothe, repair, feed, clean, or contain the previous thing, not merely evade it, outlast it, or repeat it at greater size.
sketches.move_shape: Name your night-shift answer and its action: "I am a sedative, quieting the restless patient." A sedative beats restlessness.
sketches.first_card: I am a blaring alarm, shaking the sleeping ward.

sketches.title: Discharge Orders
sketches.premise: Every turn writes a new hospital order for the problem currently standing in the room. The order must become a real thing that acts on that problem, and the judge signs it only if the cure is clearer than the paperwork.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes what stands by directly undoing its harm, blocking its function, or taking it away; escape, resistance, and a more extreme version of the same thing are all rejected.
sketches.move_shape: Write the order aloud: "I am an ice pack, cooling the burn." An ice pack beats a burn.
sketches.first_card: I am a deep cut, opening the skin.
